question: How many readings of a bill take place in the legislative process?
solution: Second reading is the most important stage for the future of the bill.

question: To whom does the Governor address his resignation letter?
options: To the Speaker of the Assembly
solution: The Governor continues to hold office even after the end of his term until his successor assumes office.

question: In which article is the Governor's right to address the House and send messages?
solution: The Governor can also send messages regarding pending bills.

question: Whose constitutional duty is it to give information to the Governor under Article 167?
solution: The Chief Minister has to give information about both administrative and legislative proposals.

question: Who presents the budget in the state legislature?
solution: The budget is always presented by the Governor.

question: By whom are the salaries and allowances of officers of the Legislature determined?
options: According to Article 186, the state legislature decides their salaries by making a state law.
solution: The salaries of these officers are paid from the consolidated fund of the state.

question: What can be the maximum and minimum number of members of the Assembly respectively?
solution: The members of the Legislative Assembly are elected directly by the public.

question: By which constitutional amendment was the provision made to appoint the same person as the Governor of two or more states?
solution: This amendment helped in reducing the administrative and financial burden.

question: Under which article discussion on the conduct of judges in the Legislature is prohibited?
solution: This is to maintain the independence and respect of the judiciary.

question: Under which article is the annual financial statement of the state presented?
solution: The annual financial statement is commonly called budget.

question: In which Article it is provided that the executive power of the State shall extend to the subjects on which the State Legislature can make laws?
solution: The executive power of the State also applies to the subjects of the Concurrent List, provided there is no contrary law of the Centre.

question: Which article of the Constitution states the duties of the Advocate General?
solution: The Advocate General provides legal advice to the state government.

question: How many Union Territories have their own Legislative Assembly?
solution: The Chief Ministers of Delhi and Puducherry are appointed by the President.

question: When is a special address given by the Governor?
options: At the beginning of each session
This is a mandatory address under Article 176 in the first session after the general elections and in the first session of every year.
This is not required during an emergency.
solution: This address contains details of the policies and future programs of the government.

question: What can the Governor do instead of withholding his assent to a Money Bill?
options: Can send legislation to the Council
solution: Normally the Governor gives his assent to the Money Bill because it is introduced with his prior permission.

question: Who determines the salaries of ministers according to Article 164?
solution: The salaries and allowances of ministers are paid from the consolidated fund of the state.

question: According to Article 177, which right do the Ministers and the Advocate General do not have in the House?
solution: The Advocate General can participate in the proceedings of both the Houses but he does not have the right to vote in either House.

question: If there is a difference of opinion between the two Houses in the matter of an ordinary bill, can a joint meeting be called?
options: Only on the insistence of the Chief Minister
solution: The Legislative Council can only delay the Bill, not stop it.

question: Which bill must the Governor mandatorily reserve for the President?
options: Which reduces the powers of the High Court
Only those bills which the Chief Minister says
solution: This is a safeguard mechanism to maintain the independence of the judiciary.

question: With which officer of the Center can the Advocate General of the State be compared?
solution: Both are the chief legal advisors of the government at their respective levels.

question: Minimum presence of how many members is required for quorum in the House?
options: One fifth of the total members
One-tenth of the total members or 10 members whichever is more
solution: If there is no quorum, the Speaker is forced to adjourn the House.

question: How long does the Advocate General remain in his post?
options: According to Article 165(3), the Governor can remove him at any time as per the pleasure of the Governor.
Till the tenure of the assembly
solution: The remuneration of the Advocate General is determined by the Governor.

question: Which bill is mandatory to be passed to withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund?
solution: The Appropriation Bill is the final stage of the budget process.

question: Which statement is true regarding the Legislative Council?
options: All its members are elected together
One-third of its members retire every 2 years
solution: The individual tenure of the members of the Legislative Council is 6 years.

question: Which language is used for communication between one state and another?
options: Official language of the Union: According to Article 346, the official language is used for mutual communication.
solution: Two states can make Hindi the language of communication with mutual consent.

question: What does the Governor use in appointing the Chief Minister in the event of a hung assembly?
options: Of the opinion of the Supreme Court
Chief Minister's advice is not possible when the post is vacant.
solution: This work of the Governor should be fair and transparent.

question: What proportion of the members of the Legislative Council are elected by the Legislative Assembly members?
solution: These members are elected from among persons who are not members of the Legislative Assembly.

question: What is the main difference between the pardon power of the Governor and the President?
options: The Governor can change the orders of the court martial
President can pardon the death penalty
The powers of both are exactly the same. There is a difference in the scope and powers of both.
The Governor can completely pardon the death penalty
solution: The Governor can only ask for postponement or reconsideration of the death penalty.

question: In which article the pardoning powers of the Governor are described?
solution: The Governor can grant pardon for offenses committed against the law of the state.

question: What is the minimum number of members in Nagaland Assembly?
solution: Nagaland has special status under Article 371A.

question: Subordinate Courts are mentioned in which group of articles of the Constitution?
options: Articles 153 to 167 are for the executive.
solution: District judges are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Court.

question: By whom can the Governor be removed from his post?
solution: The Constitution does not mention any specific reason or procedure for removal.

question: Within how many days does the Legislative Council have to return the Money Bill?
solution: The Legislative Council can suggest amendments to the Money Bill but it is up to the Assembly to accept them.

question: What does the last article of the Constitution that ends Part 6 relate to?
solution: The High Court has control over the subordinate courts.

question: Apart from the Governor, who else is included in the Legislature of each state?
solution: Most of the states in India have only one house i.e. Legislative Assembly.

question: How much fine can one have to pay per day for participating in the proceedings of the House without taking oath?
solution: This fine can be recovered as a debt payable to the state.

question: Which condition for the post of Governor is not mentioned in the Constitution?
options: He must be a citizen of India
He must have completed 35 years of age
He should not hold any office of profit
He should not be a resident of the state of which he is the Governor.
solution: According to tradition, the Chief Minister is consulted at the time of appointment of the Governor.

question: What is the minimum number of members of the Legislative Council?
solution: Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council has the highest number of members in India.

question: How many members of the Legislative Council are nominated by the Governor?
solution: This nomination is done to give representation to specific sections of the society.

question: In which article is it mentioned that the entire executive power of the state will be vested in the Governor?
solution: All executive functions of the state are formally performed in the name of the Governor.

question: What will happen to a Minister who is not a member of the Legislature for a continuous period of 6 months on the expiry of that period?
options: He will be dismissed by the Governor
He will no longer be a minister
He will have to be removed by the Chief Minister
solution: This provision allows an outsider to become a minister temporarily.

question: If the same person is appointed as the Governor of two states, who decides his salary?
options: Chief Ministers of the respective states
solution: The salary of the Governor is charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.

question: In the matter of budget and financial procedures, how many articles of Parliament are added to get the articles of State?
solution: Article 112 deals with the Union Budget and by adding 90 to it we get Article 202 which deals with the State Budget.

question: How many states in India currently have bicameral legislature?
options: This number is less in 5 states.
solution: In a bicameral system, the Legislative Assembly is called the lower house and the Legislative Council is called the upper house.

question: Which of the following is not a part of the State Executive under Articles 153 to 167?
solution: The Governor is the formal head of the state while the Chief Minister is the de facto head.

question: In which article has the provision for imparting education in mother tongue at the primary level been added?
solution: This is important for the right to education and maintaining linguistic identity.

question: Can the Courts inquire into the proceedings of the Legislature?
options: Only on the orders of the Chief Minister
Only with the permission of the President
solution: The decision of the Presiding Officer taken within the House is final.

question: Before whom does every member of the Legislature have to take oath before assuming his office?
options: The Chief Minister himself takes the oath before the Chief Minister.
This is a constitutional requirement under Article 188 before the Governor or his appointee.
Before the Speaker of the Assembly
solution: Taking part in the proceedings of the House without taking oath is a punishable offence.

question: When does the Presiding Officer get the right to vote in the House?
options: Only in case of equality of votes, according to Article 189(2), he has the right to cast only the casting vote.
solution: This is also called casting vote.

question: Who appoints the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?
solution: This post was created after the state reorganization of 1956.

question: Under which article of the Constitution the law creating or abolishing the Legislative Council is not considered an amendment?
solution: It can be implemented through the ordinary legislative process.

question: How many members can the Governor nominate to the Legislative Council?
solution: The nomination made by the Governor cannot be challenged in the court.

question: How much time does the Legislative Council get to consider a Money Bill?
solution: If the Council makes any suggestion, the Assembly is not bound to accept it.

question: Under which article is it the duty of the Union to promote and develop Hindi?
solution: Its objective is to make Hindi a medium of expression of the composite culture of India.

question: In which article there is provision for supplementary, additional or higher grant?
solution: It provides flexibility to the government for unexpected expenses.

question: The suggestions of the Assembly Legislative Council in case of ordinary bill?
options: Can be accepted only after 6 months
solution: The Legislative Council acts only as a delaying house.

question: In which article is it mentioned that there will be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister as its head to aid and advise the Governor?
solution: The advice of the Council of Ministers is binding on the Governor, except in cases where he has to act in his discretion.

question: During the discussion on the budget, which part is only for discussion and cannot be voted on?
solution: This has been done to ensure economic independence of constitutional posts.

question: Under which article does the State Legislature make the rules of its functioning?
solution: The rules of the House are to maintain the dignity and discipline of the House.

question: What is necessary for a candidate to contest assembly elections?
options: It is not mandatory to be a resident of that state, but it is necessary to be a voter.
It is mandatory to have the person's name in the voter list as a registered voter of the concerned constituency.
solution: A person can contest elections from two constituencies simultaneously.

question: According to Article 158, which condition is mandatory for the post of Governor?
options: He does not hold any office of profit
He must be a member of Parliament
He must be a resident of the state
solution: If an MP becomes the Governor, he has to give up his membership before assuming office.

question: How many years is the tenure of the members of the Legislative Council?
solution: Every two years one-third of the members leave and new members come.

question: Who decides the discharge of the functions of the Governor in certain extenuating circumstances under Article 160?
solution: If the post of Governor suddenly becomes vacant, the President can hand over the charge to the Chief Justice of the High Court.

question: In which House of the Legislature an Ordinary Bill can be introduced?
options: Only in the Legislative Council the Council has limited powers.
solution: For the bill to become law, it is necessary to be passed by both the Houses and assent of the Governor.

question: Who has the right to create or abolish the Legislative Council?
options: The Assembly has to first pass the resolution by a special majority.
According to Article 169, the Parliament can create or abolish the Legislative Council by a simple majority.
solution: To abolish the Legislative Council, a resolution of the Legislative Assembly of the concerned state is mandatory.

question: If the Speaker of the Assembly wishes to tender his resignation, to whom will he address?
solution: This arrangement shows the autonomy of the House.

question: Which committee is formed to consider the report of the Official Language Commission?
options: Joint Parliamentary Committee on Official Language
solution: This committee consists of 20 Lok Sabha and 10 Rajya Sabha members.

question: According to which article of the Constitution there will be a Governor for each state?
solution: The original Constitution provided for a separate Governor for each state.

question: Who has the right to choose the official language of the state?
options: According to Article 345, the State Legislature can choose any regional language or Hindi as its official language by making a state law.
solution: If the state does not choose a language, English continues to be used.

question: Which qualification is mandatory for the appointment of Advocate General of the State?
options: He should be a relative of the Chief Minister
It is not necessary that he should have been an MLA for at least 10 years.
He should be qualified to become a judge of the High Court
He should be the Attorney General of India
solution: The Advocate General is the first law officer of the state.

question: By what method are the members of the Legislative Council elected?
options: Indirect election: They are elected by proportional representation through single transferable vote.
solution: Through this method, representation of different groups is ensured.

question: What is Part 6 of the Indian Constitution mainly related to?
solution: Part 6 of the Constitution is also called the Constitution of the States.

question: How long after the commencement of the session of the Legislature does the Governor's Ordinance automatically expire?
solution: If the Legislature disapproves an ordinance, it ceases to be effective immediately.

question: If a member of the Legislature remains absent without notice for how many days, his seat can be declared vacant?
solution: The time of prorogation or adjournment of the House is not included in the calculation of this period.

question: What is the maximum gap that can be between sessions of the Legislature?
solution: The Governor summons and adjourns the session of the House from time to time.

question: Which statement is true regarding demands for grants?
options: These cannot be done without the recommendation of the Governor
These are placed directly before the public
They can also be presented in the Legislative Council
solution: Voting takes place in the Assembly on budget expenditure but not on expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund.

question: In which article is the power of the Governor to issue ordinances given?
solution: The power of an ordinance is the same as that of a law made by the Legislature.

question: Which option does not the Governor have with respect to the Bill under Article 200?
options: Sending the bill directly to the Supreme Court
It is his prerogative to reserve the bill for the consideration of the President.
solution: The Governor can once again send back an ordinary bill for reconsideration.

question: According to Article 166(3), who makes the rules for the functioning of the State Government?
solution: This is done for the smooth functioning of the state administration.

question: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor?
options: Chief Justice of the High Court
solution: In the absence of the Chief Justice, the senior most available judge of the High Court administers the oath.

question: If a question arises on the discretion of the Governor, whose decision is considered final?
options: According to Article 163(2), the decision of the Governor is final and cannot be challenged.
solution: The discretion of the Governor is an important constitutional power.

question: When does the Speaker of the Assembly cast his vote?
options: When the votes for and against are equal, it is called a decisive vote.
solution: To maintain complete impartiality in the House, the Speaker generally remains silent.

question: What is the number of members in Mizoram Assembly?
solution: Mizoram gained full statehood in 1987.

question: Who performs the functions of the Chairman of the Legislative Council when his post becomes vacant?
solution: The Chairman submits his resignation in writing to the Deputy Chairman.

question: What is a bill called after it is given assent by the Governor?
options: The proposal is put up for discussion.
solution: The Act is required to be published in the Official Gazette.

question: What type of power is the power of the Governor to issue ordinances?
solution: Ordinances can be issued only on subjects on which the Legislature can make laws.

question: The Governor has to pay rent for his residence?
options: Only if the salary is reduced
solution: The official residence of the Governor is called Raj Bhavan.

question: What is the minimum number of assembly members fixed in Goa, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh?
solution: Special provisions have been made in the Constitution for small states.

question: According to Article 348, what will be the language of the courts until a law is made by the Parliament?
solution: Parliament will have to make a special law to remove English.

question: Which is the equivalent post of President at the state level?
solution: The Governor is considered the first citizen of the state.

question: In which article is the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council mentioned?
solution: The Chairman of the Legislative Council submits his resignation to the Deputy Chairman.

question: In which part of the Constitution are the provisions related to the official language given?
solution: The Department of Official Language works under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

question: According to Article 156, what is the tenure of the Governor?
options: During the pleasure of the President
solution: The grounds for removal of the Governor are not mentioned in the Constitution.

question: The official language of the Union will be Hindi and the script will be Devanagari, in which article is this?
solution: Hindi was accepted as the official language on 14 September 1949.

question: In which article the privileges of the members of the State Legislature are given?
solution: Members cannot be held accountable in court for anything they say during the proceedings of the House.

question: If a proposal to remove the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker is under consideration, what cannot they do?
options: Cannot vote in the first instance
Cannot be present in the House
solution: This is necessary to maintain fairness.

question: Who elects the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly?
solution: The Chairman submits his resignation letter to the Deputy Chairman and the Vice Chairman submits his resignation letter to the Chairman.

question: For how many years was English allowed for official purposes after the Constitution came into force?
solution: The use of English was extended indefinitely through the Official Language Act 1963.

question: What does Article 152 of the Constitution clarify?
solution: This definition applies to the provisions covered by Part 6.

question: When does the Vice President act as the President?
options: When the post of the Speaker is vacant or he is absent
When the Speaker is on leave
solution: If the posts of both are vacant, the member appointed by the Governor acts as the Chairman.

question: How many states can a Governor take charge of after the 7th Constitutional Amendment?
options: According to the amendment, he can look after the responsibility of any number of states.
solution: In such cases the salary burden is shared by the respective states.

question: Can the Governor be a member of both the Houses of the Legislature simultaneously?
options: This can be done with the permission of the Chief Minister
He can only be a member of the Legislative Council
solution: If he is a member, his seat will be considered vacant as soon as he assumes office.

question: In which article is the language used in the state legislature mentioned?
solution: The Speaker may allow a member to speak in his mother tongue.

question: According to the Constitution, whose constitutional responsibility is it to administer the oath of office to the Governor?
options: It is clearly written in Article 159 of the Chief Justice of the High Court.
solution: The format of the oath is not mentioned in the Third Schedule of the Constitution but in Article 159 itself.

question: Who has the power to dissolve the assembly?
options: The President has the power to impose President's rule only in the state.
The Chief Minister can only make recommendations.
The Governor has the power to dissolve the Assembly prematurely under Article 174(2).
The Speaker of the Assembly only has the power to adjourn the meeting of the House.
solution: The Legislative Council is a permanent house, hence it can never be dissolved.

question: In which article of the Constitution are the instructions for the development of Hindi language given?
solution: The government should make Hindi a language in which all the elements of India's mixed culture can be expressed.

question: What can the President do with a bill under Article 201?
options: He can direct the Governor to return the bill
He can send it to the Supreme Court
solution: He can sit indefinitely on a bill sent to the President.

question: The tenure of the Legislative Assembly is usually how many years from its first meeting?
solution: During an emergency the term of the Assembly can be extended for one year at a time.

question: It is the duty of the Chief Minister to inform the Governor of all the decisions of the Council of Ministers, in which article is this mentioned?
solution: The Governor can seek information from the Chief Minister on any administrative matter.

question: Whose advice does the Governor have to take before deciding on questions of disqualification?
options: The High Court intervenes only in legal disputes.
According to Article 192 of the Election Commission, the Governor will act only according to the opinion of the Election Commission.
solution: The opinion of the Election Commission is binding on the Governor.

question: The total number of members of the Legislative Council should not exceed what part of the Legislative Assembly of that state?
solution: The number of members of the Legislative Council should be at least 40.

question: Under which article does the Governor get the power to withdraw money from the "Contingency Fund"?
solution: After this, it is necessary to take post-facto approval from the Legislature.

question: What can be the maximum number of elected members of the Legislative Assembly?
solution: At present Uttar Pradesh Assembly has the highest number of members.

question: When President's rule is imposed in a state, whose representative does the Governor act as?
options: The High Court can only give legal advice.
solution: In such a situation the Chief Secretary acts as the chief advisor to the Governor.

question: What is the minimum age limit set for the post of Governor?
solution: There is no mention of any educational qualification for the Governor in the Constitution.

question: In which article instructions for linguistic minorities are mentioned?
solution: These provisions were added in 1956 at the time of reorganization of states on linguistic basis.

question: In whose name are all executive functions of the state government formally performed?
options: In the name of the Chief Secretary
In the name of the President
In the name of the Chief Minister
In the name of the Governor
solution: The Governor makes rules for the more convenient conduct of the functions of the State Government.

question: To match the articles of the Center and the State, how much is added to Articles 73 to 111 to get the corresponding articles of the State Legislature?
solution: Article 74 has the Council of Ministers and by adding 89 to it we get Article 163 which is about the State Council of Ministers.

question: Who can make special provision for a language spoken by a section of the population of a State under Article 347?
solution: This is to protect the interests of linguistic minorities.

question: When is vote on account used?
options: When the budget is not passed on time
solution: It is also called vote on account.

question: How many members are elected by the local bodies in the Legislative Council?
solution: Local bodies include representatives of Panchayats and Municipalities.

question: In which article is it mentioned that the Chief Minister will be appointed by the Governor?
solution: Other ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.

question: Which group does not participate in the election of members of the Legislative Council?
solution: Graduates must have obtained the degree at least 3 years prior.

question: In which article is the Consolidated Fund of the State described?
solution: Approval of the Legislature is necessary to withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund.

question: How many members are elected by graduates and teachers in the Legislative Council?
solution: For this, the bachelor's degree should be 3 years old.

question: Under which article the Secretariat of the State Legislature is constituted?
solution: The conditions of service of the Secretariat are determined by the Legislature.

question: What is wrong regarding the ordinance power of the Governor?
options: It can be withdrawn at any time
Its effect is equal to law
This can be issued only when the House is not in session
solution: The decision to issue an ordinance is taken on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

question: What will happen if a person is elected a member of both the Houses of the State Legislature?
options: The Governor will decide where he will live
He has to vacate one House seat
He can remain a member of both
Both his memberships will be cancelled.
solution: No person can be a member of both Parliament and State Legislature at the same time.

question: To whom is the State Council of Ministers collectively responsible?
options: According to Article 164(2), it is mandatory for the Council of Ministers to have the confidence of the Assembly.
This is the principle of personal responsibility towards the Governor.
solution: If the no-confidence motion is passed in the Assembly, the entire Council of Ministers has to resign.

question: What should be the minimum age to become a member of the Legislative Assembly?
solution: This age limit has been kept the same as that of a Lok Sabha member.

question: Which article contains special provisions regarding financial bills?
solution: A financial bill also cannot be introduced without the recommendation of the Governor.

question: What is the formula to remember states with bicameral legislature?
solution: The names of six states can be easily remembered with this formula.

question: In which Chapter of Part 6 of the Constitution are the provisions related to High Courts?
solution: Provision for a High Court for each State is made in Article 214.

question: If the Legislative Council rejects an ordinary bill passed by the Assembly, then for what maximum period can the Council block it?
solution: There is no provision for joint sitting in the state legislature.

question: In which chapter the details of the state executive are given under Part 6?
solution: The state executive consists of the Governor, Chief Minister, Council of Ministers and Advocate General.

question: Which post in the state is equivalent to the Attorney General of the Central Government?
solution: The Advocate General holds his post during the pleasure of the Governor.

question: In which article is it written that the tenure of the Governor is 5 years?
solution: However, he can be removed by the President even before 5 years.

question: According to Article 164(3), who administers the oath of secrecy to the ministers?
solution: Ministers take two types of oaths – of office and of secrecy.

question: In which article is it mentioned what will be the language of the Supreme Court and High Courts?
solution: The Governor can, with the consent of the President, permit the use of Hindi in High Court proceedings.

question: In which state's case did the Supreme Court say that the Governor should not postpone decisions on bills indefinitely?
solution: The Court stressed that the delay hampers the legislative process.

question: Who decides the disqualification of a member on the basis of defection?
options: Speaker or Chairman of the House
solution: Anti-defection law was added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment.

question: In which House is a Money Bill compulsorily introduced?
options: There is no provision for such a meeting in a joint meeting.
solution: Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Legislative Council.

question: In which article the definition of Money Bill is given?
solution: The Speaker of the Assembly decides whether a bill is a money bill or not.

question: In which article it is stated that the emoluments and allowances of the Governor cannot be reduced during his tenure?
solution: This provision is to ensure the independent functioning of the Governor.

question: What is the similarity between the pardon power of the Governor and the power of the President?
options: Both can pardon the death penalty
Only the President can pardon the sentences of both military courts.
Both can grant amnesty for violations of foreign laws
Both can reduce or change the punishment
solution: The Governor can grant pardon only on matters which fall within the executive power of the state.

question: When was the first Official Language Commission formed and who was its Chairman?
solution: The work of this commission was to suggest the development of Hindi as an official language.

question: Who casts his casting vote in case of equality of votes on any bill in the Assembly?
options: The most senior member of the House
solution: Under normal circumstances the Speaker remains impartial and does not vote.

question: What is the minimum age limit for membership of the Legislative Council?
solution: Apart from age, the person must also be a citizen of India.

question: What is not a ground for disqualification from membership under Article 191?
options: Being of unsound mind or bankrupt is a ground for disqualification.
Acquiring citizenship of a foreign state
solution: The decision of disqualification on the basis of defection is taken by the Speaker or Chairman.

question: By whom is the Governor appointed?
options: Appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
solution: The post of Governor in India is appointed rather than elected.
